completion_conditions: A task in planned or ready whose expected_pr names an already-merged PR gets a fresh implementation, not a closeout.
A task in review whose expected_pr is merged still drives the closeout exactly as today.
The stale pointer is detected from the task record alone.
The full suite, the goal-loop suite, the adversarial-state suite and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: MEASURED. Amendment PR #308 changed task T-20260806T065143409817Z-dbdae1cf's design from 'stage the coordinator mirror' to 'commit it', because staging had been proven not to clear a non-fast-forward merge. The loop was re-dispatched against the amended contract and its entire history was: cycle 1 `dispatch` ('task is ready for the implementer runtime'), cycle 2 `create_closeout_pr` ('impl PR merged; push completion to main via a closeout PR'). `git log -- scripts/shiki_loop.py` showed ONE commit for that task, from BEFORE the amendment. The closeout (#309) changed only `.shiki` files. The amended contract was never implemented, and nothing detected it.

CAUSE, read from source. `decide_task_action` (`scripts/shiki_loop.py:259-267`) treats a merged `expected_pr` as proof this cycle's implementation is done: `if pr_state.get('merged'):` -> `mark_done` when `closeout_pr` is set, else `create_closeout_pr`. The task's `expected_pr` was 309 — the loop repoints `expected_pr` at the closeout PR during a closeout — so after the amendment re-opened the task, the pointer still described the PREVIOUS cycle.

CONFIRMED BY THE FIX. Clearing `expected_pr` by hand and re-dispatching produced a real implementation on the next run: 279 insertions / 102 deletions across three files, including the `git commit` the amendment required. Nothing else changed.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. An amendment is the only sanctioned way to correct a frozen contract. If the loop can silently skip the implementation of an amended contract, the amendment mechanism does not work — the mirror records a corrected contract that no code satisfies, and the CCA confirms `complete`. This session used amendments three times; this happened on one of them.

THE RULE, and its failure direction. A task in `planned` or `ready` whose `expected_pr` names an ALREADY-MERGED PR is carrying a stale pointer from a previous cycle: no work has been dispatched for the current one. Treat it as absent and cut a fresh implementation, rather than reading it as this cycle's completed work. Failing the other way — clearing a pointer that was still live — would at worst re-open a PR-less cycle and re-implement, which the loop already handles; reading a stale pointer as done silently ships nothing, which is what happened.

DO NOT infer re-opening from an amendment marker, a ledger scan, or PR timestamps. The condition is local and self-evident from the task record itself: a non-terminal status plus a merged `expected_pr` cannot both describe the current cycle.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK (2026-08-07). MUST-CHANGE: `scripts/shiki_loop.py` (the decision at `:259-267`); `tests/test_loop_engine.py` and `tests/test_closeout.py`, the two files that drive `decide_task_action` through the merged-`expected_pr` branch and would otherwise pin the old behaviour; `tests/test_reopened_task.py` (new).

MUST-NOT-BREAK (verification command, not locks): `tests/test_branch_behind_sync.py`, `tests/test_loop_verdict_gating.py`, `tests/test_repair_delivery.py`, `tests/test_session_lease.py`, `tests/test_lock_conflict_stop.py` — all drive `decide_task_action` but none through a merged `expected_pr` on a non-terminal status; `scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh` and `scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh`, which drive the loop end to end; and `scripts/mergegate_check.py`, `scripts/shiki_evidence.py`, `scripts/guardian_approval_signal.py`, which READ `expected_pr` and must keep reading it unchanged.

Risk is medium: this changes one decision inside the loop. No gate, schema, workflow or approval source moves. Under `.shiki/guardian-policy.json` (`applies_to_risk: [high, critical]`) neither PR triggers the Guardian gate.

tasks.scope:
In `scripts/shiki_loop.py`'s `decide_task_action`, stop reading a previous cycle's PR pointer as this cycle's completed work.

MEASURED 2026-08-06. Amendment PR #308 changed task `T-20260806T065143409817Z-dbdae1cf`'s design from staging the coordinator mirror to committing it — because staging had been proven not to clear a non-fast-forward merge. The loop was re-dispatched against the amended contract and its ENTIRE history was:
  cycle 1  dispatch             'task is ready for the implementer runtime'
  cycle 2  create_closeout_pr   'impl PR merged; push completion to main via a closeout PR'
`git log -- scripts/shiki_loop.py` showed one commit for that task, from BEFORE the amendment; the closeout (#309) changed only `.shiki` files. The amended contract was never implemented, and the CCA returned `complete`.

CAUSE: `:259-267` treats a merged `expected_pr` as proof the implementation is done — `if pr_state.get('merged'):` -> `mark_done` when `closeout_pr` is set, else `create_closeout_pr`. The task's `expected_pr` was 309, the CLOSEOUT PR, because the loop repoints `expected_pr` during a closeout. After the amendment re-opened the task, that pointer still described the previous cycle.

THE RULE: a task whose status is `planned` or `ready` and whose `expected_pr` names an ALREADY-MERGED PR is carrying a stale pointer — no work has been dispatched for the current cycle. Treat the pointer as absent and cut a fresh implementation. A task in `review` with a merged `expected_pr` is unchanged: that is the normal path into the closeout, and it must keep working exactly as today.

Detect it from the TASK RECORD ALONE — a non-terminal status plus a merged `expected_pr` cannot both describe the current cycle. Do NOT infer re-opening from an amendment marker, a ledger scan or PR timestamps.

FAILURE DIRECTION, and why this way round: clearing a pointer that was still live at worst re-opens a PR-less cycle and re-implements, which the loop already handles. Reading a stale pointer as done silently ships nothing — which is what happened, through a CCA that confirmed `complete`.

TESTS. `tests/test_reopened_task.py` (new): a `ready` task with a merged `expected_pr` decides to cut a fresh implementation, not `create_closeout_pr`; the same for `planned`; a `review` task with a merged `expected_pr` still decides `create_closeout_pr`; a `review` task with `closeout_pr` set and a merged `expected_pr` still decides `mark_done`; an UNMERGED `expected_pr` on a non-terminal task is untouched. `tests/test_loop_engine.py` and `tests/test_closeout.py` drive `decide_task_action` through this branch and pin the old behaviour — update them without weakening any closeout assertion, and add the measured sequence: an amended, re-opened task must not reach `create_closeout_pr` on its first cycle.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: a Spec Amendment merges, the loop is re-dispatched, and it produces no implementation at all — straight to a closeout whose diff contains no source change. The mirror then records a corrected contract that no code satisfies, and the CCA confirms `complete`.
  Measured 2026-08-06 on PR #308 / task T-20260806T065143409817Z-dbdae1cf, with the two-cycle history above.
  Root cause: `shiki_loop.py:259-267` reads a merged `expected_pr` as this cycle's completed implementation, and the loop repoints `expected_pr` at the closeout PR, so the pointer survives the re-open pointing at the previous cycle.
  Confirmed by the fix: clearing `expected_pr` by hand and re-dispatching produced a real implementation on the next run — 279 insertions / 102 deletions across three files, including the change the amendment required.
  Why it matters more than its size: an amendment is the only sanctioned way to correct a frozen contract. If its implementation can be silently skipped, the mechanism does not work.
  Reproducible when: a re-opened task with a merged `expected_pr` cuts a fresh implementation, and the ordinary `review` -> closeout path is unchanged.
